## 1. The subdomain list

> Here are the 16 subdomains under `vision`. What is missing? What is a distinction nobody in your field actually makes? What are we calling by the wrong name?

(03 §12.2, ask 1.) The family: Benchmarks whose input or output is visual and whose scored quantity is a property of that visual signal.

- Included: Tag this as PRIMARY if the score measures what was recovered from, or produced as, an image, video or 3D signal.
- Excluded: Do NOT tag this if the scored relation is between a visual signal and language -- a question answered about an image, an expression grounded in a scene, a caption retrieved for a photo -- which is \`multimodal\`. A text prompt that merely conditions generation does not make a benchmark multimodal; the discriminant is whether crossing between the modalities is what is scored. Do NOT tag it as primary either where overhead imagery is labelled with Earth-system quantities (\`earth-climate/remote-sensing\`), or where medical images carry clinically defined targets against a clinician reference standard (\`medicine-health\`), although the metric is a vision metric; the vision task subdomain is then secondary.

### 2.1 ImageNet (imagenet)

`data/benchmarks/vision/imagenet.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-10-14 · last verified 2026-10-14

*ILSVRC's 1,000-class image classification benchmark (ImageNet-1k), scored by top-1 and top-5 accuracy.*

The ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC) classification benchmark, run by the ImageNet team (Stanford, Princeton and collaborators) as a yearly challenge from 2010 to 2017. Its 2012 data, kept unchanged through 2017 and now called ImageNet-1k, is a 1,000-class subset of ImageNet: 1,281,167 training, 50,000 validation and 100,000 test photographs collected from Flickr and other search engines and labelled with the help of Amazon Mechanical Turk workers, one label per image. A system returns up to five class labels per image in descending order of confidence. From 2012 the challenge ranked by top-5 error, the share of images whose label is not among the five; top-1 error uses the first label alone. The test labels are withheld and scored by the maintainers' server at most twice a week, while the validation labels are released, and papers now report top-1 accuracy computed on their own (as\_used). One trained annotator's top-5 error on 1,500 test images was estimated at 5.1%. The same images carry a single-object localisation task (a subset here).

#### imagenet · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/classification · [S3][imagenet-s3]
  - why: The headline task assigns each whole photograph to classes from a fixed set of 1,000, scored against its one ground-truth label.
  > Task 1: Classification For each image, algorithms will produce a list of at most 5 object categories in the descending order of confidence.
- `capability` = perception · [S3][imagenet-s3]
  - why: The input is a photograph and the score is whether the object class recovered from it matches the label.
  > The general goal is to identify the main objects present in images.
- `evaluation_method` = exact-match · [S6][imagenet-s6]
  - why: Each image has one ground-truth label, and a prediction is right or wrong. Top-1 asks whether the first label equals it and top-5 whether any of five does, and the score is the mean over images. Since 2012 there is no partial credit; the hierarchical cost of 2010 and 2011 was dropped.
  > Thus, since ILSVRC2012 we have been exclusively using the top-5 metric which is the simplest and most suitable to the dataset
- `designed_for_subjects` = task-specific-supervised-model · [S6][imagenet-s6]
  - why: Entrants are classifiers trained on the benchmark's own training split and run on the test images as trained, from pipelines of hand-designed features and linear classifiers to the convolutional networks that won from 2012.
  > Participants train their algorithms using the training images and then automatically annotate the test images.

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `vision/detection` · [S4][imagenet-s4]
  - why: The challenge's object detection task (200 fully labelled classes, from 2013) and video detection task used their own data and are not covered here. Single-object localisation on the same images is a subset, with detection as its own primary domain.
  > Object localization for 1000 categories. Object detection for 200 fully labeled categories. Object detection from video for 30 fully labeled categories.
- `capability` not `distribution-shift-generalization` · [S5][imagenet-s5]
  - why: The validation and test images were collected and labelled like the training images. Test sets built to shift that distribution, such as ImageNetV2, are benchmarks of their own (lineage).
  > We build new test sets for the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets.

(field `activity`) activity is unknown because the Kaggle competition (the 2017 page's successor channel) and the image-net.org test server (behind a login) could not be read. closed fits if the maintainers' 2017 handover ended the series and the server is a private scoring service; leaderboard-live-no-round fits if Kaggle's board still takes entries. · [S4][imagenet-s4]

2. (field `lifecycle`) Saturation is derived and was not set. Are we done with ImageNet? (arXiv 2006.07159) finds the original labels nearing the end of their usefulness; whether claims now support headroom\_consumed \>= 0.95 on top-1 accuracy needs the claims the derivation reads. · [S8][imagenet-s8]
   > indicating that their usefulness in evaluating vision models may be nearing an end
3. (field `data.access`) The facets describe the design (test labels withheld, server-scored), so data.access is train-open-test-held-out and the tier not-independently-reproducible. If the validation set that papers use is taken as the headline, access becomes gated-registration (the copies read need a login or click-through; Kaggle's terms were not read) and the tier fully-automatable.
4. (field `evaluation_method`) exact-match for top-5, where an image counts as right if any of five labels equals its one label; the term's inclusion test speaks of a response equal to the reference.
5. (field `governance.independence_flags`) funded-by-evaluated-party rests on the paper's thanks to Google for sponsoring the challenges and on its team table placing GoogLeNet under Google, whose garbled text layer reads only as below; sponsorship of the challenges is read here as funding. · [S6][imagenet-s6]

### 2.2 ADE20K (ade20k)

`data/benchmarks/vision/ade20k.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-10 · last verified 2026-11-10

*Scene parsing of everyday photographs into 150 stuff and object classes, scored by mean IoU and pixel accuracy.*

A densely annotated dataset of about 25,000 photographs of everyday scenes from MIT CSAIL, covering the scene categories of the SUN database, in which a single expert annotator labelled every object and stuff region, object parts and parts of parts, with an open vocabulary of thousands of classes. From it the maintainers built the MIT Scene Parsing Benchmark (SceneParse150): the 150 classes with the largest pixel share (35 stuff and 115 object classes), 20,210 training and 2,000 validation images with public masks, and a held-out test set scored by an evaluation server on the mean of pixel accuracy and mean IoU. It ran as the Scene Parsing Challenge with ILSVRC 2016 and again in the Places Challenge 2017, which added an instance segmentation benchmark on 100 object classes (InstSeg100) scored by COCO-style mask AP. The full dataset was re-released in 2021 with 25,574 training images, 3,688 categories and blurred faces and licence plates. In practice papers report single- or multi-scale mean IoU on the 2,000 validation images, and the evaluation server no longer runs.

#### ade20k · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/segmentation; secondary vision/detection · [S1][ade20k-s1]
  - why: The headline benchmark assigns one of 150 classes to every pixel of a photograph and scores the labelling against the annotator's masks, which is the segmentation leaf's definition. The InstSeg100 benchmark detects and masks individual object instances and is scored by COCO-style AP, which is the detection leaf, secondary (and the subset's primary). Nothing is scored against language, so the multimodal boundary (02 S11 rule 12) is not in question for the benchmark the maintainers run.
  > Scene parsing is to segment the whole image densely into semantic classes, where each pixel is assigned a class label such as the region of tree and the region of building.
- `capability` = perception · [S6][ade20k-s6]
  - why: Both benchmarks score what was recovered from a photograph -- a class for every pixel, or each object instance's mask and class -- against the reference annotation.
  > For each image, segmentation algorithms will produce a semantic segmentation mask, predicting the semantic category for each pixel in the image.
- `evaluation_method` = domain-metric · [S1][ade20k-s1]
  - why: Mean IoU over the 150 classes is named in domain-metric's own test, and the paper lists pixel accuracy beside it among the metrics commonly used for semantic segmentation; the instance benchmark uses COCO's mask AP. The challenge's final score averages pixel accuracy and mean IoU, two measures of one per-pixel labelling against one key, so it is not composite (see review\_checks).
  > Mean IoU indicates the intersection-over-union between the predicted and ground-truth pixels, averaged over all the classes.
- `designed_for_subjects` = task-specific-supervised-model · [S2][ade20k-s2]
  - why: The benchmark releases training masks for its 150 classes, and its baselines and challenge entrants are segmentation networks trained on them; the 2016 challenge allowed only ImageNet and Places365 pre-training beside the provided data.
  > you can use pre-trained models trained on the standard 1.2M imagenet data and the Places365 data

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `multimodal/visual-grounding` · [S4][ade20k-s4]
  - why: Open-vocabulary segmentation papers score ADE20K-847 and ADE20K-150 by naming the classes in text to a vision-language model, but that is how another group's derivative is used (see lineage\_note); the maintainers' benchmark fixes the 150 class indices and scores masks only.
  > on the ADE20K-847 benchmark
- `domain` not `vision/image-generation` · S5
  - why: The papers synthesise scenes from label masks and remove objects by inpainting, but only as applications of trained parsers; no generated image is scored.
  > We further show that the trained scene parsing networks can lead to applications such as image content removal and scene synthesis
- `evaluation_method` not `composite` · [S7][ade20k-s7]
  - why: The final score is the mean of pixel accuracy and mean IoU, but both are computed from the same per-pixel predictions against the same masks, which composite's exclusion keeps out as one method; papers now report mean IoU alone.
  > Final score = (Pixel-wise Accuracy + mean(Intersection over Union)) / 2
- `evaluation_method` not `classification-metric` · [S1][ade20k-s1]
  - why: Pixel accuracy is the share of labelled pixels classified correctly, but it is reported beside mean IoU as a segmentation measure, and classification-metric's exclusion sends IoU and mAP to domain-metric.
  > Pixel accuracy indicates the proportion of correctly

### 2.3 Kinetics (kinetics)

`data/benchmarks/vision/kinetics.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-08 · last verified 2026-11-08

*DeepMind's human action benchmark of 10-second YouTube clips in 400 to 700 classes, scored by top-1 and top-5 accuracy.*

A series of human action video classification datasets from DeepMind, each a list of about ten-second clips cut from distinct YouTube videos and labelled with one action class after Amazon Mechanical Turk workers confirmed it. Kinetics-400 (2017) has 400 classes and 306,245 clips; Kinetics-600 (2018), 600 classes and 495,547 clips; Kinetics-700 (2019), 700 classes and 650,317 clips; and Kinetics-700-2020 replenished the rarest classes to at least 700 clips each. Each edition has train, validation and test splits, and the score is top-1 and top-5 accuracy on held-out clips; the ActivityNet challenge ran it as its trimmed-video task from 2017 to 2021, ranked by the mean of top-1 and top-5 error. The maintainers distribute YouTube identifiers and time spans, not videos, so clips vanish as videos are removed (about 3% a year). The Common Visual Data Foundation mirrors the videos. Papers mostly report top-1 accuracy on the Kinetics-400 validation split.

**Evidence** (53 quoted fields), by checklist area:

#### kinetics · Identity and id

- `self_description` · [S1][kinetics-s1]
  > We describe the DeepMind Kinetics human action video dataset.
- `released` = 2017-05-19 · [S1][kinetics-s1]
  > Submitted on 19 May 2017

#### kinetics · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/video-understanding · [S2][kinetics-s2]
  - why: Each item is a short video clip, and what is scored is the one action label recovered from it, with no language to correspond to. That is video-understanding's case (action recognition), and under 02 S11 rule 12 the class name is the label, not a text the clip is matched against.
  > Each clip is human annotated with a single action class and lasts around 10 seconds.
- `capability` = perception · [S4][kinetics-s4]
  - why: The input is a raw video clip and the score is whether the human action recovered from it matches the clip's label.
  > The dataset is focused on human actions (rather than activities or events).
- `evaluation_method` = exact-match · [S4][kinetics-s4]
  - why: Each clip has one ground-truth label and a prediction is right or wrong. Top-1 asks whether the first label equals it and top-5 whether any of five does, and the score is the mean over clips. The paper prefers top-5 because a clip can show actions it is not labelled with. The challenge averaged the top-1 and top-5 errors, one method at two values of k, which is not composite.
  > a top-5 measure is more suitable than top-1
- `designed_for_subjects` = task-specific-supervised-model · [S4][kinetics-s4]
  - why: The entrants are video classifiers trained on the edition's own training split and run on its held-out clips; the release baselines are trained from scratch on it.
  > For the experiments on the Kinetics dataset all three architectures are trained from scratch using Kinetics.

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `multimodal/video-language` · [S3][kinetics-s3]
  - why: No question, caption or description is scored against the video. The challenge's metric compares predicted class labels with the one ground-truth label, which video-language's own distinction leaves with vision/video-understanding.
  > Please take into account that only 5 predictions are allowed per video.
- `domain` not `audio-speech/audio-event-understanding` · [S4][kinetics-s4]
  - why: The clips keep their soundtrack and the maintainers mention multimodal use, but the score is the human action class, not a sound event. Audio was allowed as an input in the 2021 challenge, which leaves it an input only.
  > the clips also contain sound so the dataset can potentially be used for many purposes, including multi-modal analysis
- `capability` not `temporal-reasoning` · [S5][kinetics-s5]
  - why: Some classes need motion to tell apart, but correctness never depends on when things happened relative to one another. The maintainers say the collection favours actions that last the whole clip over ones with a beginning, middle and end.
  > It is very well suited to continual actions that exist over the length of the video
- `capability` not `transfer-learning` · [S6][kinetics-s6]
  - why: Kinetics-pretrained models are carried to other video datasets, but that transfer is scored on those datasets. The maintainers' 2020 note only expects Kinetics to become a downstream task.
  > Kinetics may eventually become, in turn, a good downstream task itself
- `capability` not `distribution-shift-generalization` · [S7][kinetics-s7]
  - why: The 2021 challenge's self-supervised track trained on a subset of classes to test out of domain generalisation, but that is one track (a subset), not the headline.
  > to test for out of domain generalization
- `evaluation_method` not `composite` · [S8][kinetics-s8]
  - why: The challenge's ranking figure averages top-1 and top-5 error, both the same per-clip verdict at different k, which composite's exclusion test keeps out.
  > The performance criterion used in the challenge is the average of Top-1 and Top-5 error.

**Open review checks** (10):

1. (field `versions`) Identity. One entry with Kinetics-400, -600, -700 and -700-2020 as editions, because one maintainer issued all four on the same task with new clips and a growing class list, and the 2020 note calls them editions. Each edition is still cited and reported in its own right, Kinetics-400 most of all, which is 04 S4's test for a separate benchmark ("independently versioned and cited"). The supersedes chain records order only; no edition is marked superseded\_by. · [S6][kinetics-s6]
   > Three editions have been released: Kinetics-400 \[6\], Kinetics-600 \[1\] and Kinetics-700 \[2\]
2. (field `versions`) Kinetics-700-2020 as an edition rather than a revision. It keeps Kinetics-700's classes and mostly its clips, topping up the 123 rarest classes and removing some clips, which is close to revision's "same items, changed contents". The maintainers' own word is edition. · [S6][kinetics-s6]
   > Note, unlike in previous years we have not increased the number of classes.
3. (field `data.access`) data.access fully-open is judged on the splits papers report (a validation split, or Kinetics-400's released test labels). If the current edition's test split decides (fully-open's rule for families), Kinetics-700-2020's CVDF test list carries no labels, which gives train-open-test-held-out and reproducibility not-independently-reproducible. · [S14][kinetics-s14]
   > youtube\_id,time\_start,time\_end,split
4. (field `activity`) activity unknown. No challenge has run since 2021 and the evaluation server is behind a login. closed fits if the server no longer scores; leaderboard-live-no-round if it still takes held-out-test submissions.
5. (field `execution.reproducibility_blockers`) Vanishing clips are recorded as task\_distribution\_drifts and in the tier note, not as the live-world-state blocker, following audioset; tier 3 forbids that blocker beside fully-automatable. · [S5][kinetics-s5]
   > since YouTube videos are deleted or unlisted over time (about 3% per year)
6. (field `governance.maintainer`) maintainer DeepMind as an industry-lab. The papers present it as DeepMind's, and the dataset page licensed the data in Google Inc.'s name; CVDF and ActivityNet host copies and tools. Whether CVDF's mirror makes it a co-maintainer was not settled.
7. (field `governance.independence_flags`) independence not assessed. The maintainers' own I3D baselines appear in every note; the challenge entrant lists for 2017, 2018, 2020 and 2021 were not read.
8. (field `data.dataset_licence`) dataset\_licence CC-BY-4.0 rests on a 2023 Wayback capture of the maintainer's page; no live page states it now, and the YouTube videos' and CVDF mirror's terms are unstated. · [S2][kinetics-s2]
   > The kinetics dataset is licensed by Google Inc. under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.
9. (field `lineage`) Kinetics-derived datasets the maintainer page lists beside the editions (AVA-Kinetics, Countix, Compressed Kinetics600) are not recorded as variants; they carry other tasks on Kinetics videos. Mini-Kinetics and Kinetics-Sounds were not looked at.
10. (field `lifecycle`) Saturation is derived and was not set. Kinetics-400 top-1 in the 2026 papers read is around 80 to 83%, but the non-exhaustive labels leave the ceiling unknown.

### 2.4 ETH3D (eth3d)

`data/benchmarks/vision/eth3d.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-08 · last verified 2026-11-08

*Multi-view and two-view stereo and SLAM on real scenes, scored against laser scans and motion capture by a server.*

A benchmark from ETH Zurich for dense stereo reconstruction from real indoor and outdoor scenes, with ground truth geometry from a laser scanner (CVPR 2017). It has three stereo scenarios: high-resolution multi-view stereo on 24-megapixel DSLR images, low-resolution many-view stereo on videos from a four-camera rig, and low-resolution two-view stereo on rectified frames of the same rig. Calibrated cameras are given. Multi-view reconstructions are submitted as point clouds and scored by accuracy, completeness and their F1 score against the laser scan over thresholds from 1 cm to 50 cm, with 2 cm the default; two-view disparity maps are scored by the Middlebury bad-pixel and error metrics. A SLAM benchmark was added in 2019 with the BAD SLAM paper: RGB-D, stereo and monocular visual-inertial video from synchronised global-shutter cameras, with motion-capture ground truth, scored by trajectory error. Training ground truth is public; test ground truth is withheld and scored by an online server, which also asks for each method's runtime. In October 2017 the test set was replaced by new scenes and the first test set became training data. Learned stereo and MVS networks now enter beside classical PatchMatch pipelines, and papers also reuse the data for monocular depth and offline SLAM evaluation.

**Evidence** (51 quoted fields), by checklist area:

#### eth3d · Identity and id

- `self_description` · [S1][eth3d-s1]
  > Motivated by the limitations of existing multi-view stereo benchmarks, we present a novel dataset for this task.
- `released` = 2017-07-19 · [S2][eth3d-s2]
  > 2017-07-19: Initial release of the dataset.
- `release_venue` = CVPR 2017 · [S3][eth3d-s3]
  > "event":{"name":"2017 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)","location":"Honolulu, HI","start":{"date-parts":\[\[2017,7,21\]\]}

#### eth3d · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/multi-view-stereo; secondary vision/depth-geometry · [S1][eth3d-s1]
  - why: The benchmark was built to evaluate stereo algorithms with calibrated views given, and two of its three stereo scenarios score dense multi-view reconstructions against laser scans, which is the multi-view-stereo leaf. The two-view scenario scores a disparity per pixel of a rectified pair, which is depth-geometry, secondary. The SLAM benchmark scores camera trajectories, for which no vision leaf exists; its subset carries 3d-reconstruction as the nearest leaf and the gap is logged (see review\_checks). Nothing is scored against language, so the multimodal boundary (02 S11 rule 12) is not in question.
  > Our benchmark consists of three scenarios corresponding to different tasks for (multi-view) stereo algorithms
- `capability` = perception · [S6][eth3d-s6]
  - why: Every scenario scores how accurately geometry, depth or camera motion was recovered from images of a real scene, against a laser scan or motion capture of it.
  > Ground truth geometry has been obtained using a high-precision laser scanner.
- `evaluation_method` = domain-metric · [S1][eth3d-s1]
  - why: The multi-view score is accuracy and completeness computed per voxel against the laser scan, with unobserved space modelled from the scanner's beams and only scan points seen in two images used, and their F1 score at a distance threshold; the two-view score is the Middlebury bad-pixel rates; the SLAM score is SE(3) ATE RMSE. Each is a measure defined within its field (see review\_checks).
  > Only laser scan points visible in at least two images are used for evaluation.
- `designed_for_subjects` = classical-algorithm, task-specific-supervised-model · [S1][eth3d-s1]
  - why: The 2017 paper evaluates four classical MVS pipelines (PMVS, Gipuma, COLMAP, CMPMVS) and five two-view methods, one of them learned (MC-CNN), and releases training scenes with ground truth; it argues that its variety matters given the popularity of learning-based methods. The 2019 SLAM baselines are classical SLAM systems tuned on the training datasets.
  > The latter is especially important given the popularity of learning-based methods
- `evaluation_target` = mixed · [S7][eth3d-s7]
  - why: The benchmark was built to evaluate classical stereo and MVS pipelines, which are entrants, not baselines, and classical PatchMatch methods still sit beside learned networks on the high-res board; DiffMVS reports a traditional method as the one its learned network matches on the test set.
  > compared with HPM-MVS \[29\], the state-of-theart traditional method, CasDiffMVS achieves competitive performance on the test set
- `secondary_axes` = latency · [S4][eth3d-s4]
  - why: Runtime per dataset is mandatory with every submission and shown on the boards beside the score.
  > we are interested in the methods' runtimes and request these as mandatory information for each submission

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `vision/3d-reconstruction` · [S4][eth3d-s4]
  - why: The 3d-reconstruction leaf's own note keeps multi-view stereo apart as benchmarked with calibrated views given, and ETH3D gives each scene's calibration, unlike Tanks and Temples, which withholds it and scores complete SfM+MVS pipelines. The site does call the scenarios a 3D reconstruction benchmark; the SLAM subset uses the leaf as its nearest (see review\_checks).
  > The calibration is provided in the format of the COLMAP Structure-from-Motion program.
- `domain` not `vision/image-matching-correspondence` · [S4][eth3d-s4]
  - why: The two-view scenario matches pixels between the images of a rectified pair, but the scored quantity is the disparity map against laser-scan ground truth, which is depth-geometry; no correspondence set is scored.
  > The two-view datasets provide stereo-rectified image pairs
- `domain` not `robotics-embodiment/navigation` · [S5][eth3d-s5]
  - why: The SLAM benchmark was recorded with a hand-held camera rig and scores trajectories estimated from the recorded video; no agent acts or moves through an environment.
  > can be used to evaluate visual-inertial mono, stereo, and RGB-D SLAM
- `capability` not `distribution-shift-generalization` · [S7][eth3d-s7]
  - why: The paper argues its varied scenes reward general solutions, and learned stereo and MVS networks are now entered zero-shot after synthetic or DTU training, but the benchmark defines no shifted condition of its own; training on its public training data is allowed.
  > Both sets are commonly used to test the zero-shot generalization ability of learning-based MVS methods
- `evaluation_method` not `classification-metric` · [S8][eth3d-s8]
  - why: F1 is in its list, but here it is computed from point-to-point distances to a laser scan at a threshold, not from predicted labels, as the term's Tanks and Temples near miss records.
  > F1 score \[%\]: The harmonic mean of accuracy and completeness, used to rank methods based on both metrics.
- `evaluation_method` not `statistical-fit` · [S9][eth3d-s9]
  - why: The two-view board also reports average and RMS disparity error, and the SLAM score is an RMSE, but the ranked two-view measure is the bad-pixel rate and ATE RMSE after SE(3) alignment is SLAM's own named metric, which the term's exclusion sends to domain-metric.
  > we focus on the absolute trajectory RMSE with SE(3) alignment

#### eth3d · Task and evaluation

- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system WAFT-Stereo · [S10][eth3d-s10]
  > it achieves the best BP-0.5 on the ETH3D benchmark among all existing submissions
- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system CasDiffMVS · [S7][eth3d-s7]
  > our CasDiffMVS achieves the best performance among the learning-based methods on both training and test sets
- `reproducible_by_third_party` = true · [S13][eth3d-s13]
  - why: Anyone can download the data, run the published evaluation programs on the training scenes and sequences, and submit test results to the server. The test scores themselves come only from the server.
  > For evaluating training results locally, the evaluation program is provided as source code (on GitHub).
- `task` = exists true; input calibrated, undistorted (or original distorted) DSLR images of one scene, high-res multi-view, calibrated video frames from a four-camera rig, low-res many-view, a stereo-rectified image pair from the rig, low-res two-view, an RGB-D, stereo or monocular video with IMU data, SLAM; output A point cloud per scene (PLY) for the multi-view scenarios, a disparity map per frame (PFM) for two-view, or a camera trajectory per sequence for SLAM, each with the method's runtime, uploaded as one archive.; scoring Multi-view point clouds are scored against the laser scan by accuracy, completeness and F1 over thresholds from 1 cm to 50 cm, averaged per voxel and per category; two-view disparities by bad-pixel rates (0.5 to 4 px), average and RMS error and error quantiles; SLAM trajectories by ATE RMSE after SE(3) alignment. A category is averaged and ranked only when every dataset in it has a result.; metric_range 0, 100 · [S4][eth3d-s4]
  > For the multi-view scenarios, results should be provided as binary PLY files having the same name as the dataset, with the extension .ply.
- `execution.reproducibility_tier` = not-independently-reproducible · [S9][eth3d-s9]
  - why: The headline scores are on the test sets, which only the server can produce because it holds their ground truth. Training-set scores can be reproduced offline with the published programs.
  > It includes a training set, a test set without public ground truth, and an online evaluation service.
- `execution.harness` = ETH3D multi-view-evaluation (C++, PCL), with the two-view-evaluation and slam-evaluation programs, for the training data; Windows binaries are also offered · [S16][eth3d-s16]
  > This tool is used for evaluating multi-view reconstruction methods in the \[ETH3D benchmark\](https://www.eth3d.net/).
- `execution.submission_channel` · [S4][eth3d-s4]
  > To submit your results, you need to sign up for an account and login.
- `aggregation_policy` = official-aggregate · [S4][eth3d-s4]
  - why: Category averages are the official aggregate, computed only for complete categories.
  > Partial submissions are possible, but we only compute category averages (and therefore rank a method in a category) if results for all of the datasets within a category are provided.

#### eth3d · Data and licence

- `as_used` = protocol Learned two-view stereo networks trained only on synthetic data are submitted to the test server zero-shot, and ablations are scored offline on the public training frames. The benchmark allows training on its training data; the zero-shot label is the papers' own, not a track of the benchmark.; split low-res two-view, test and training · [S10][eth3d-s10]

- `lifecycle` = active · [S10][eth3d-s10]

**Open review checks** (10):

1. (field `domain`) Primary is multi-view-stereo with depth-geometry secondary. Tanks and Temples (tanks-and-temples) is the related entry and differs on the point that decides the leaf. It withholds calibration and scores complete SfM+MVS pipelines from video (3d-reconstruction primary), while ETH3D gives COLMAP calibration and scores binocular stereo and MVS (multi-view-stereo primary). ETH3D also adds a two-view scenario, rig video from robotics-grade cameras with autoexposure, and SLAM. The ETH3D paper itself calls the two benchmarks complementary. 3d-reconstruction as a secondary is the alternative, since the site calls the scenarios a 3D reconstruction benchmark. · [S1][eth3d-s1]
   > While our benchmark focuses on evaluating both binocular stereo and MVS, theirs jointly evaluates Structure-from-Motion (SfM) and MVS.
2. (field `subsets`) The SLAM subset scores camera trajectories (ATE), for which vision has no leaf; 3d-reconstruction is carried as the nearest and a missing-term gap was logged (proposed vision/visual-slam-odometry). Whether the SLAM benchmark, introduced by a different paper with different sensors and ground truth, should be a benchmark of its own rather than a subset brought in by a track-set version; same maintainer, same site and same submission system argue for the subset. · [S2][eth3d-s2]
   > 2019-06-16: Added the SLAM Benchmark.
3. (field `versions`) The October 2017 extension is modelled as an edition (new test items for the same task; the old test set became training data). Board results submitted before it were on a different test set and are not comparable; whether the board kept or re-scored them is not shown by the sources read. · [S14][eth3d-s14]
   > We added 12 high-res multi-view datasets, 5 low-res many-view datasets, and 20 two-view stereo datasets.
4. (field `evaluation_method`) domain-metric is assigned although its exclusion names F1 and RMSE as general-purpose statistics. The multi-view F1 is computed with beam-based free-space modelling and voxel normalisation, the two-view rank is Middlebury's bad-pixel rate and SLAM's ATE follows an SE(3) alignment, as for Tanks and Temples' F-score; statistical-fit or classification-metric are the alternatives. · [S1][eth3d-s1]
   > We thus discretized the space into voxels with small side length.
5. (field `governance.independence_flags`) maintainer-competes-on-own-benchmark rests on the BAD SLAM paper, which introduced both the SLAM benchmark and its authors' own SLAM system and reports that system winning; whether it is listed on the live SLAM board was not read. The 2017 paper's baselines include MVS tools whose cited author lists overlap with the benchmark's authors, and the 2025 DiffMVS paper shares a senior author with it; neither is flagged, because no source read states the relation. · [S9][eth3d-s9]
   > our proposed algorithm outperforms all other evaluated SLAM methods
6. (field `governance.independence_flags`) The stereo paper names partial funding from Google Tango (and a Google PhD fellowship for its first author). funded-by-evaluated-party is not set, since no source read shows a Google system evaluated on the boards. · [S1][eth3d-s1]
   > This project was partially funded by Google Tango.
7. (field `activity`) Only the high-res multi-view board's default view was read, and it is withheld from archiving because its method rows carry author names. The many-view, two-view and SLAM boards are unread, so activity rests on the documentation and on WAFT-Stereo's June 2026 test submission; unknown is the alternative for the SLAM board. · [S8][eth3d-s8]
   > Tolerance: 2cm 1cm 2cm 5cm 10cm 20cm 50cm
8. (field `events`) Only the 2018 Robust Vision Challenge is evidenced. The board's \_ROB suffix suggests later rounds drew on the benchmark too, but no Robust Vision Challenge page was read. · [S8][eth3d-s8]
   > Methods with suffix \_ROB may participate in the Robust Vision Challenge.
9. (field `capability`) The headline uses in 2025-2026 are zero-shot generalisation tests (synthetic-only stereo, DTU and BlendedMVS-trained MVS), monocular depth on ETH3D's images and offline SLAM on training sequences. The facets follow the design (training data allowed, server-scored test sets); whether the zero-shot use should add distribution-shift-generalization, as the papers' framing suggests. · [S10][eth3d-s10]
   > We follow the benchmark protocols and report BP-0.5, BP-1, and BP-2 on both all pixels and non-occluded pixels
10. (field `data.ceiling_anchor_type`) The ground truth was built with the open dataset pipeline, so its construction is inspectable, but the pipeline's depth-image registration was not used for the benchmark and the laser-scan registration accuracy was assessed only qualitatively in the paper; no ceiling below 100 is recorded. · [S18][eth3d-s18]
   > which was not used for the ETH3D benchmark

### 2.5 MPI Sintel (mpi-sintel)

`data/benchmarks/vision/mpi-sintel.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-10 · last verified 2026-11-10

*Optical flow on frames rendered from the open source film Sintel, scored by endpoint error on withheld test flow.*

An optical flow benchmark from the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems (ECCV 2012), built from the open source 3D animated short film Sintel. Because the film's production data is open, the ground-truth flow of every frame was computed from the 3D scenes with a modified Blender, and the same 35 clips (1,628 frames at 1024x436) were rendered in passes of rising difficulty: Albedo, Clean (shading and specular reflections) and Final (adding motion blur, defocus blur and atmospheric effects, close to the released film). The clips are split into 23 training sequences with public flow and 12 test sequences whose flow is withheld. Entrants compute flow for every test frame of the Clean and Final passes, subsample it with the maintainers' Bundler and upload it; the server ranks methods by average endpoint error (EPE) over all frames, with breakdowns for matched and unmatched pixels, distance from motion boundaries and speed, on one board per pass. Two test sequences are perturbed to detect submissions of reconstructed ground truth. Uploads are limited and public entries must be described in a document. In 2015 the maintainers added depth and camera-motion, stereo disparity and segmentation training data, which no board scores. Learned flow networks now lead both boards; the training data and the depth releases are also reused offline for camera-pose and intrinsic-image evaluation.

#### mpi-sintel · Identity and id

#### mpi-sintel · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/image-matching-correspondence; secondary vision/depth-geometry · [S3][mpi-sintel-s3]
  - why: The scored output is a dense optical flow field, a correspondence for every pixel of one frame in the next, and the ranked score is its endpoint error against the ground-truth flow on both boards, which is the image-matching-correspondence leaf (finding corresponding points between images of the same scene), as for KITTI's flow boards. The 2015 depth and stereo disparity releases give per-pixel depth and disparity for the training sequences, which is depth-geometry, secondary; no board scores them (see review\_checks). Nothing is scored against language, so the multimodal boundary (02 S11 rule 12) is not in question.
  > rank each method on these according to average endpoint error (EPE) across all test sequences
- `capability` = perception · [S5][mpi-sintel-s5]
  - why: Every scored quantity is how accurately motion was recovered from the rendered frames, against ground-truth flow computed from the film's 3D scenes.
  > The flow for these sequences is withheld for evaluation purposes.
- `evaluation_method` = statistical-fit · [S7][mpi-sintel-s7]
  - why: The ranked score is the average endpoint error, the mean Euclidean distance in pixels between estimated and ground-truth flow vectors, averaged over all test frames; the breakdowns are the same error over the paper's masks (matched and unmatched pixels, distance bands from motion boundaries, speed bands). A mean error against ground-truth continuous values is the statistical-fit term (see review\_checks).
  > Since the sequences differ in length, the average we compute is the average over all frames, and not the average of per-sequence average errors.
- `designed_for_subjects` = classical-algorithm, task-specific-supervised-model · [S3][mpi-sintel-s3]
  - why: The paper seeds the board with six public, hand-designed flow methods (Classic+NL, Classic++, LDOF, Horn and Schunck, H-L1) and releases a training set more than a hundred times Middlebury's for learning-based methods; learned networks trained on it and on other synthetic data now lead both boards.
  > and a larger training set for machine learning methods
- `evaluation_target` = learned-system · [S10][mpi-sintel-s10]
  - why: The benchmark was seeded with classical methods, which remain on the boards, but learned networks hold the top ranks of both passes and the classical seeds now sit near the bottom of 561 rows (LDOF at 523 on the Final board, 9.116 EPE).
  > LDOF \[523\] 9.116 5.037 42.344

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `vision/video-understanding` · [S3][mpi-sintel-s3]
  - why: The inputs are video sequences and the paper encourages methods that integrate over many frames, but the score is a per-pixel motion vector against ground truth, not a recognised action, event or temporal segment, which is what the leaf scores.
  > This should encourage the development of methods that use longer sequences and integrate information over time.
- `domain` not `vision/3d-reconstruction` · [S4][mpi-sintel-s4]
  - why: Papers now score camera trajectories on Sintel clips (as\_used), but the benchmark's own score is two-dimensional image motion; no reconstruction or pose is scored by the maintainers.
  > On the common Sintel protocol, an image-free constant-velocity line has a lower mean ATE than 10 of 11 recent models re-run with official code
- `domain` not `vision/segmentation` · [S1][mpi-sintel-s1]
  - why: A segmentation training set was released beside depth and stereo in 2015, but it has no test set or board and is not modelled as a subset.
  > Please see the dedicated pages for Stereo and disparity, Depth and camera motion, and Segmentation.
- `capability` not `distribution-shift-generalization` · [S6][mpi-sintel-s6]
  - why: The Final pass is harder than Clean and papers report zero-shot transfer to and from Sintel, but the benchmark defines no shifted condition of its own and allows training on its own training set; a 2026 study finds Sintel progress predicts real-world accuracy only weakly (see review\_checks).
  > progress on Sintel, KITTI and Spring only weakly predicts accuracy on real-world data
- `evaluation_method` not `domain-metric` · [S3][mpi-sintel-s3]
  - why: Endpoint error is named and used only in optical flow and stereo, and its unmatched and boundary-distance masks are the benchmark's own definitions, which argues for domain-metric (KITTI's flow outlier percentage was tagged so). It is nonetheless a mean distance between vectors, the kind of general statistic the term's exclusion sends to statistical-fit.
  > we compute the average error in areas closer than 10 pixels, between 10 and 60 pixels, and larger than 60 pixels

- `governance.independence_flags` = flag single-evaluator-private-test-set · [S5][mpi-sintel-s5]

#### mpi-sintel · Lifecycle and activity

- `lifecycle` = active · [S9][mpi-sintel-s9]
  - why: Results are still produced against the instrument. The Final and Clean boards list FreeFlow, an ECCV 2026 paper of September 2026, first among the submissions, and 2026 papers report Sintel test results and use its data offline.

- `activity` = accepting-submissions · [S7][mpi-sintel-s7]
  - why: The FAQ still sets upload limits and explains how to submit, and a September 2026 paper's results stand first on both boards. No source says the server has closed.

- `events` = name Robust Vision Challenge 2018 (ROB), whose flow challenge drew on the Sintel benchmark; the Final board still lists ROB baseline rows; kind challenge · [S10][mpi-sintel-s10]

**Open review checks** (10):

1. (field `domain`) Primary is image-matching-correspondence (dense flow scored by EPE), with depth-geometry secondary for the 2015 depth and stereo releases, which no board scores. Whether an unscored training release should carry a secondary leaf at all, or whether depth-geometry should rest only on the offline camera-pose use (as\_used); video-understanding was rejected because nothing is recognised. · [S1][mpi-sintel-s1]
   > Please see the dedicated pages for Stereo and disparity, Depth and camera motion, and Segmentation.
2. (field `versions`) The 2015 depth, stereo and segmentation training data is modelled as a track-set version with two unscored subsets (scored\_separately false). It adds no scored item, so the alternative is no version at all, as ETH3D's added training depth maps were treated; the segmentation data is left out of the subsets. · [S14][mpi-sintel-s14]
   > This is the beta version of the dataset, and might change in the near future.
3. (field `evaluation_method`) statistical-fit rather than domain-metric for endpoint error. EPE is the field's own named measure (KITTI's flow outlier rate was tagged domain-metric), but it is a mean vector distance; the masks for unmatched pixels and boundary distance are the benchmark's own. · [S3][mpi-sintel-s3]
   > nearly 8.5% of the pixels in Sintel are unmatched
4. (field `governance.submission_process`) publication-gated rests on the FAQ's rule that every public method be described in a document, but the rule allows a document withheld during review, and many board rows are Anonymous with no paper; how strictly it is enforced was not read. · [S7][mpi-sintel-s7]
   > We reserve the right to remove methods from the public tables if there is insufficient documentation
5. (field `governance.independence_flags`) maintainer-competes-on-own-benchmark is not set. The paper's seed methods include Classic+NL, whose cited paper shares an author with the benchmark by the reference list, and the board keeps it; whether a reference row counts as competing was not decided, and no source states the relation. · [S10][mpi-sintel-s10]
   > Classic+NL \[524\] 9.153 4.814 44.509
6. (field `data.contamination_risk`) The ground-truth reconstruction risk is mitigated by two perturbed test sequences, but whether the perturbed results are still published on the board, and whether the Bundler's subsampling of the submitted flow is what the server scores, were not read on the boards. · [S3][mpi-sintel-s3]
   > Another novelty of our data set is the use of perturbed sequences for fraud detection.
7. (field `data.dataset_licence`) The film's own licence (described in the drafting brief as CC BY, Blender Foundation; not verified) is not stated in any source read, and the site's licence page claims Max-Planck ownership of "the SINTEL Software/Data"; how the two relate for redistribution of the rendered frames is for a reviewer. No SPDX id fits the site's terms. · [S13][mpi-sintel-s13]
   > The Data & Software may not be reproduced, modified and/or made available in any form to any third party without
8. (field `as_used`) Current use is mostly papers reporting zero-shot or fine-tuned results and reusing the data offline (camera pose, intrinsic images), with a 2026 study finding that Sintel progress predicts real-world flow accuracy only weakly and a pose audit finding the Sintel trajectories too straight for ATE. Whether the latter uses should lower confidence in the depth-geometry secondary or add a validity note. · [S4][mpi-sintel-s4]
   > The true path's straightness flags Sintel and Lightspeed.
9. (field `events`) Robust Vision Challenge events rest on baseline rows on the Final board only; no Robust Vision Challenge page was read, so which editions used Sintel is not confirmed. · [S10][mpi-sintel-s10]
   > RVC 2020 baseline submission
10. (field `versions`) The board's numbers for the seed methods differ slightly from the paper's Table 1 (LDOF Final 9.116 on the board, 9.15 in the paper); whether the server was re-run or the paper rounded is not stated, and the site links a corrected PDF without saying what changed. · [S10][mpi-sintel-s10]
   > LDOF \[523\] 9.116 5.037 42.344

**Reviewer checklist** for `mpi-sintel`:

- [ ] Identity and id: the name, aliases, id, paper and release date are right, and this is one benchmark, not a family or an edition of another
- [ ] Domain and capabilities: the primary and secondary subdomains, capabilities, evaluation methods and intended subjects fit, and no rejected term should have been kept
- [ ] Task and evaluation: the task, scoring, ground truth, entrants and harness read as the sources describe them
- [ ] Data and licence: access, refresh, provenance, sizes, subsets, contamination and licences match the sources
- [ ] Governance and independence: maintainer type, submission process, funding and independence flags are right
- [ ] Lifecycle and activity: lifecycle, activity, versions, editions and history are current
- [ ] Every open review check above is answered or resolved
- [ ] Nothing here would embarrass the catalogue in front of a specialist

### 2.6 NTIRE Challenges (ntire)

`data/benchmarks/vision/ntire.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-10-14 · last verified 2026-10-14

*Yearly CVPR workshop challenges since 2017 on image and video restoration and enhancement, each track ranked on its own.*

The challenges of the New Trends in Image Restoration and Enhancement (NTIRE) workshop, held with CVPR every year since 2017; the workshop itself began at ACCV 2016. The 2017 edition had one challenge, example-based single-image super-resolution on the new DIV2K dataset, in a bicubic and an unknown-degradation track at three scales. By 2026, the workshop's eleventh edition, the line-up had grown to 47 tracks on Codabench: super-resolution (x4, efficient, mobile, light field, 3D content, remote-sensing infrared), denoising, deblurring, dehazing, low-light enhancement, HDR, shadow, reflection and raindrop removal, face and video restoration and, beside them, deepfake and AI-generated image detection, few-shot object detection, depth estimation, saliency prediction and image quality assessment. Each challenge has its own organisers, data, metric and Codabench competition. Participants train on released data, get feedback from a validation server, then submit outputs on test inputs whose ground truth stays with the organisers, together with a fact sheet describing the method and the code, which the organisers use to check or re-run the entries. The restoration tracks read are ranked by PSNR against the hidden reference images, the perceptual ones by a weighted sum of learned image-quality metrics. Each challenge's results and its top teams' methods appear in a report in the CVPR Workshops proceedings, co-authored by its organisers and participants.

#### ntire · Identity and id

- `self_description` · [S1][ntire-s1]
  > In order to gauge the current state-of-the-art in example-based single-image super-resolution, to compare and to promote different solutions we are organizing an NTIRE challenge in conjunction with the CVPR 2017 conference.

#### ntire · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/image-restoration-enhancement; secondary vision/classification, vision/detection, vision/segmentation, vision/depth-geometry; per_edition true · [S2][ntire-s2]
  - why: Most of the 47 tracks of 2026 recover an image or video from a degraded one (super-resolution, denoising, deblurring, dehazing, low-light, HDR, shadow, reflection and raindrop removal), and the flagship restoration tracks score the result against the withheld clean reference. The workshop states the same scope.
  > Image restoration, enhancement and manipulation are key computer vision tasks, aiming at the restoration of degraded image content
- `capability` = generation-fidelity · [S3][ntire-s3]
  - why: The restoration tracks compare the produced image with the withheld reference, by PSNR and SSIM for fidelity and by learned metrics such as LPIPS and DISTS for perceptual closeness. capabilities.yaml names NTIRE as the term's example.
  > The evaluation consists of comparing the restored high-resolution images with the ground truth high-resolution images.
- `evaluation_method` = domain-metric, model-derived-metric, composite, classification-metric, statistical-fit, human-expert-eval, reference-metric, exact-match, model-graded-judge · [S3][ntire-s3]
  - why: The flagship x4 super-resolution challenge ranks its restoration track by PSNR alone; every other track names its own metric.
  > The objective is to maximize the restoration accuracy, which will be evaluated solely using
- `designed_for_subjects` = task-specific-supervised-model · [S5][ntire-s5]
  - why: The entrants are restoration networks trained or fine-tuned on the challenge's training pairs (DIV2K and LSDIR for super-resolution and denoising, extra data allowed if declared) and scored as trained; the term names image-restoration networks.
  > Pre-trained Transformer-based restoration backbones remain the dominant choice.
- `secondary_axes` = latency · [S3][ntire-s3]
  - why: Every x4 submission reports its runtime per image beside the score, and four 2026 tracks are named for efficiency (Efficient Super-Resolution, Efficient Low-Light Image Enhancement, Efficient Burst HDR and Restoration, and Light Field Image Super-Resolution Track 2 Efficiency).
  > the runtime per image (in seconds) of the solution

Considered and rejected:

- `evaluation_method` not `human-crowd-eval` · [S4][ntire-s4]
  - why: The UGC track's raters are described as professional students and workers from education and industry, read here as qualified raters. The quality-assessment tracks' MOS are labels to predict, not ratings of the entrants' outputs.
  > For subjective comparison, we organize two professional students and workers from education and industry to conduct subjective experiments for all teams.

**Open review checks** (11):

1. (field `versions`) Identity. The entry is the challenge series as one family, with editions as versions and the 2026 tracks as subsets. Long-running lines (x4 super-resolution, in its fourth edition in 2026; denoising; efficient super-resolution) could be entries of their own, and the challenges of the related AIM, MAI and AIS workshops are not included. · [S2][ntire-s2]
   > New Trends in Image Restoration and Enhancement (NTIRE) editions at: CVPR 2025 , CVPR 2024 , 2023 , 2022 , 2021, 2020 , 2019 , 2018 and 2017 and at ACCV 2016
2. (field `evaluation_method`) evaluation\_method is the union over the eight 2026 tracks read, since subsets cannot override it. Three terms (reference-metric, exact-match, model-graded-judge) rest on RAIM Track 1 alone, and human-expert-eval on the UGC track alone. A reviewer may prefer the restoration tracks' methods only.
3. (field `evaluation_method`) PSNR and SSIM are tagged domain-metric, as Stage 3 did. PSNR is a log transform of mean squared error against a reference image, so statistical-fit or reference-metric could be argued. · [S3][ntire-s3]
   > The objective is to maximize the restoration accuracy, which will be evaluated solely using
4. (field `evaluation_method`) human-expert-eval reads the UGC report's 'professional students and workers' as qualified raters; the wording is ambiguous and human-crowd-eval is the alternative. · [S4][ntire-s4]
   > For subjective comparison, we organize two professional students and workers from education and industry to conduct subjective experiments for all teams.
5. (field `subsets`) RAIM Track 1 carries multimodal/visual-qa because its reasoning text is scored against expert reviews and by an LLM judge. Quality assessment has no vision leaf (Stage 3's ntire-001, still open), so the X-AIGC tracks carry no domain\_override; vision/quality-assessment would settle all three. · [S7][ntire-s7]
   > This track challenges participants to train MLLMs that can handle high-resolution inputs and output professional-grade reasoning to predict image quality preferences.
6. (field `subsets`) The domain\_override of the rip current, depth, AI-generated image and anomaly detection tracks rests on their names (and, for anomaly detection, two accepted papers' titles); their Codabench pages were not read.
7. (field `governance.submission_process`) sandboxed-rerun. The x4 Codabench page says the final score comes from running the submitted code, but the x4 report says the results rest mainly on the Codabench uploads, with the code used for verification. The deepfake track's private test is the clear case. · [S5][ntire-s5]
   > The evaluation results are primarily determined by the submissions made to the Codabench server, while the submitted code is used for reproduction and verification
8. (field `governance.submission_process`) publication-gated rests on the mandatory fact sheet (a compiled PDF describing the method); a challenge paper is optional, and co-authorship of the report is by invitation. · [S3][ntire-s3]
   > To enter the final ranking the participants will need to fill out a survey (fact sheet) briefly describing their method.
9. (field `governance.independence_flags`) Industry teams win tracks (SamsungAICamera, first in both x4 tracks) while Samsung, OPPO, Kuaishou and Bytedance staff co-organise others and OPPO and Kuaishou sponsor. The rules let sponsors' employees be ranked; no team's affiliation was checked, so maintainer-competes is not tagged. · [S3][ntire-s3]
   > If you are an employee, affiliated with or representant of any of the NTIRE challenge sponsors then you are allowed to enter in the contest and get ranked
10. (field `data.contamination_risk`) contamination\_risk medium, where Stage 3 said low. The test references are withheld, but LSDIR's images come from Flickr and the DIV2K test split is reused, so web-scale pretraining is a plausible route. · [S5][ntire-s5]
   > dataset contains 86,991 high-quality images sourced from the Flickr platform
11. (field `activity`) activity between-rounds assumes no 2027 edition is announced; the 2027 page returned 404 on 2026-10-14. If a 2027 call with dates appears, round-scheduled applies.

**Reviewer checklist** for `ntire`:

- [ ] Identity and id: the name, aliases, id, paper and release date are right, and this is one benchmark, not a family or an edition of another
- [ ] Domain and capabilities: the primary and secondary subdomains, capabilities, evaluation methods and intended subjects fit, and no rejected term should have been kept
- [ ] Task and evaluation: the task, scoring, ground truth, entrants and harness read as the sources describe them
- [ ] Data and licence: access, refresh, provenance, sizes, subsets, contamination and licences match the sources
- [ ] Governance and independence: maintainer type, submission process, funding and independence flags are right
- [ ] Lifecycle and activity: lifecycle, activity, versions, editions and history are current
- [ ] Every open review check above is answered or resolved
- [ ] Nothing here would embarrass the catalogue in front of a specialist

### 2.7 KITTI Vision Benchmark Suite (kitti)

`data/benchmarks/vision/kitti.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-08 · last verified 2026-11-08

*Seventeen online boards on drives around Karlsruhe, from stereo, flow, depth and odometry to 3D detection and tracking.*

A benchmark suite built from one car's recordings around Karlsruhe, on rural roads and on highways, by Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago. The car carried grayscale and colour stereo cameras, a Velodyne laser scanner and a GPS/IMU unit, and the laser scans and poses give the ground truth. The suite went online in March 2012 with stereo, optical flow and visual odometry, and 2D object detection and orientation followed that August (CVPR 2012 paper; the raw recordings have their own IJRR 2013 paper). Boards added since are tracking (2013), road and lane estimation (2013), the harder stereo, flow and scene flow 2015 benchmarks on 200 dynamic scenes (CVPR 2015), 3D and bird's-eye-view object detection (2017), depth completion and single-image depth prediction (2017), semantic and instance segmentation (2018), multi-object tracking and segmentation (2019) and segmenting and tracking every pixel (2021). Each board has its own metric: the percentage of pixels whose disparity or flow error exceeds 3 px and 5 %, inverse-depth RMSE, scale-invariant log error, relative translation and rotation drift, average precision at 3D box overlap, and HOTA. Training data and labels are released; the test inputs are released without ground truth, and the cvlibs.net server scores uploaded results, three a month per benchmark. Only work aimed at a peer-reviewed paper may be submitted, and entries left anonymous or without a paper are deleted after six months. The data is under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, and downloading it needs a registered account.

**Evidence** (61 quoted fields), by checklist area:

#### kitti · Identity and id

- `self_description` · [S1][kitti-s1]
  > Our tasks of interest are: stereo, optical flow, visual odometry, 3D object detection and 3D tracking.
- `released` = 2012-03-20 · [S1][kitti-s1]
  > 20.03.2012: The KITTI Vision Benchmark Suite goes online, starting with the stereo, flow and odometry benchmarks.
- `release_venue` = CVPR 2012 · [S2][kitti-s2]
  > "name":"2012 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)"
- `lineage.variants` = id kitti-360; relation successor dataset by the same group on the same server, with new suburban recordings around Karlsruhe (73.7 km), a 360-degree fisheye, stereo and pushbroom-laser rig, its own paper (PAMI 2022) and its own boards · [S14][kitti-s14]
  > This setup is similar to the one used in KITTI

#### kitti · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/depth-geometry; secondary vision/image-matching-correspondence, vision/driving-perception-3d, vision/detection, vision/segmentation, vision/video-understanding · [S3][kitti-s3]
  - why: Counted by board, the leaves are depth-geometry 5 (stereo 2012 and 2015, scene flow, depth completion, depth prediction), segmentation 5 (road, semantics, instances, MOTS, STEP), driving-perception-3d 3 (odometry, 3D, bird's eye view), image-matching-correspondence 2 (flow 2012 and 2015), detection 1 (2D objects) and video-understanding 1 (tracking). Depth-geometry is taken over the tie with segmentation because the geometric boards (depth, flow, scene flow and odometry, 8 of 17) are the suite's founding tasks and its stated tasks of interest, and because every depth board scores a per-pixel disparity or depth map against laser ground truth; the segmentation boards were added from 2013 to 2021. What is scored is the visual signal recovered, never a relation to language, so by 02 S11 rule 12 the suite is vision.
  > Our evaluation server computes the percentage of bad pixels averaged over all ground truth pixels of all 200 test images.
- `capability` = perception · [S4][kitti-s4]
  - why: Every board scores structure recovered from raw camera, laser or GPS/IMU recordings -- disparity, flow and depth maps, camera trajectories, boxes, tracks and labels -- against laser-derived or annotated ground truth.
  > The ground truth for visual odometry/SLAM is directly given by the output of the GPS/IMU localization unit
- `evaluation_method` = domain-metric, statistical-fit · [S5][kitti-s5]
  - why: The stereo 2015 board ranks by the share of erroneous pixels, defined by KITTI's own disparity and end-point thresholds; depth completion ranks by inverse-depth RMSE.
  > Our evaluation table ranks all methods according to the root mean squared error (RMSE) of the inverse depth maps.
- `designed_for_subjects` = task-specific-supervised-model, classical-algorithm · [S4][kitti-s4]
  - why: The 2012 paper's first rankings are hand-designed stereo, flow and odometry methods, and classical lidar and visual odometry still lead that board; the stereo, depth, detection and tracking boards are now led by networks trained on the released training splits, such as the depth prediction entry OCEM.
  > For stereo matching, we run global \[26, 37, 46\], semiglobal \[23\], local \[5, 20, 38\] and seed-growing \[27, 10, 9\] methods.
- `secondary_axes` = latency · [S13][kitti-s13]
  - why: Every board lists each method's runtime and computing environment beside its score; the tracking board leaves detection time out of it so that methods compare.
  > To make the methods comparable, the time for object detection is not included in the specified runtime.

Considered and rejected:

- `capability` not `distribution-shift-generalization` · [S4][kitti-s4]
  - why: The 2012 paper's claim is that methods tuned on laboratory benchmarks fail on its real scenes, but training and test images come from the same drives, and no shifted condition is scored as its own.
  > We further ensure that images from one sequence do not appear in both training and test set.
- `designed_for_subjects` not `base-model` · [S6][kitti-s6]
  - why: Depth entries now start from large pretrained encoders (OCEM pretrains on 421 million video frames), but a task decoder is trained on top and the result is scored as trained, not prompted.
  > We adopt DCDepth \[83\] as the depth decoder and evaluate on the KITTI Eigen split \[84\], \[85\].

#### kitti · Task and evaluation

- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system OCEM (DCDepth decoder on a motion-pretrained Swin-H encoder), on the depth prediction board at 7.91 SILog · [S8][kitti-s8]
  > OCEM code 7.91 1.02 6.36 8.53
- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system OCEM · [S6][kitti-s6]
  > Our Swin-H achieves the best performance among our models, obtaining 6.36 Abs Rel, 1.02 Sq Rel, 8.53 iRMSE, and 7.91 SILog.
- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system VirConv-S, first on the 3D car detection board at 87.20 % moderate AP · [S9][kitti-s9]
  > 1 VirConv-S code 87.20 % 92.48 % 82.45 %
- `reproducible_by_third_party` = true · [S1][kitti-s1]
  - why: The development kits include the evaluation code, so training splits can be scored locally, and any registered user whose work targets a paper can submit to the servers.
  > 26.08.2012: For transparency and reproducability, we have added the evaluation codes to the development kits.
- `task` = exists true; input a rectified colour stereo pair of a road scene from the 2015 test set (optionally its neighbouring frames and the calibration); output A disparity map for the left image, one value per pixel; methods giving less than full density are filled in by background interpolation before scoring.; scoring D1-all, the percentage of ground-truth pixels whose disparity is an outlier (error above 3 px and 5 % of the true value), over all 200 test images, through the server. Other boards score their own outputs (see subsets).; metric_range 0.0, 100.0 · [S3][kitti-s3]
  > Our evaluation table ranks all methods according to the number of erroneous pixels.
- `execution.reproducibility_tier` = not-independently-reproducible · [S3][kitti-s3]

**Open review checks** (10):

1. (field `domain`) Primary depth-geometry rather than driving-perception-3d or segmentation. By board count depth-geometry and segmentation tie at five (MOTS and STEP counted as segmentation), and depth-geometry was taken because the suite's founding and stated tasks are geometric. The leaf driving-perception-3d's definition, perceiving the 3D road scene from vehicle sensors, literally covers every KITTI board; it was kept for the 3D detection and odometry boards, to keep the leaf to what nuScenes is (3D boxes and tracks in the world frame). · [S1][kitti-s1]
   > Our tasks of interest are: stereo, optical flow, visual odometry, 3D object detection and 3D tracking.
2. (field `versions`) Identity. The seventeen boards are subsets of one suite (one site, account, policy and server), and the 2015 stereo and flow boards are a track-set rather than an edition, because the 2012 boards stay open beside them. KITTI 2015 could be argued an edition of the 2012 stereo and flow boards (same tasks, new scenes, its own paper). · [S1][kitti-s1]
   > 29.07.2015: We have released our new stereo 2015, flow 2015, and scene flow 2015 benchmarks.
3. (field `lineage`) KITTI-360 is linked as a same-maintainer variant with the proposed id kitti-360. It shares the server and the copyright line, but the PAMI 2022 paper was not read, and no source read names who holds KITTI-360 now. The KITTI home page links the University of Tuebingen's Autonomous Vision group, which may be today's host of both, but no text on it says so. · [S14][kitti-s14]
   > This setup is similar to the one used in KITTI
4. (field `governance.independence_flags`) maintainer-competes-on-own-benchmark rests on OSF, the 2015 paper's method, ranked on the stereo 2015 board (also, not read, the flow and scene flow boards). The author overlap between that paper and the suite's maintainers is not quoted, by the no-names rule; a reviewer should confirm it from the paper. · [S3][kitti-s3]
   > Object Scene Flow for Autonomous Vehicles. Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2015.
5. (field `data.data_provenance`) crowd-authored rests on hired annotators and Mechanical Turk workers whom no source describes as specialists. Most of the depth, flow and pose ground truth is instrument data, so real-world-instrument is the larger share. · [S13][kitti-s13]
   > we additionally labeled the left/right boundaries of each object by making use of Mechanical Turk
6. (field `subsets`) The tracking board scores 2D image boxes over time and has no leaf; it was put under video-understanding with detection secondary, as the MOTChallenge draft does, and logged as a missing term (kitti-001; motchallenge-001 proposes the same vision/multi-object-tracking). The odometry board was put under driving-perception-3d for want of a pose leaf. · [S13][kitti-s13]
   > We evaluate 2D 0-based bounding boxes in each image.
7. (field `data.submission_limit`) submission\_limit is three a month per benchmark (2016). The 72-hour minimum gap from 2012 may still apply, and the login page asks for a single upload of a method's final setting, which is a stricter rule than the cap. · [S1][kitti-s1]
   > 26.07.2016: For flexibility, we now allow a maximum of 3 submissions per month and count submissions to different benchmarks separately.
8. (field `as_used`) as\_used rests on one paper. Depth prediction papers commonly report the Eigen split, and 3D detection papers often report a validation split of the training data; only the depth case was read. · [S6][kitti-s6]
   > We adopt DCDepth \[83\] as the depth decoder and evaluate on the KITTI Eigen split \[84\], \[85\].
9. (field `evaluation_method`) evaluation\_method leaves the road, semantic and instance segmentation boards untagged because their pages were not read; road is usually scored by an F-measure in the bird's-eye view (classification-metric) and segmentation by IoU (domain-metric).
10. (field `activity`) activity accepting-submissions reads the 2013, 2014 and 2021 workshops as events beside a board that never ran rounds. If any held a ranked challenge on a KITTI board, the value is leaderboard-live-no-round.

**Reviewer checklist** for `kitti`:

- [ ] Identity and id: the name, aliases, id, paper and release date are right, and this is one benchmark, not a family or an edition of another
- [ ] Domain and capabilities: the primary and secondary subdomains, capabilities, evaluation methods and intended subjects fit, and no rejected term should have been kept
- [ ] Task and evaluation: the task, scoring, ground truth, entrants and harness read as the sources describe them
- [ ] Data and licence: access, refresh, provenance, sizes, subsets, contamination and licences match the sources
- [ ] Governance and independence: maintainer type, submission process, funding and independence flags are right
- [ ] Lifecycle and activity: lifecycle, activity, versions, editions and history are current
- [ ] Every open review check above is answered or resolved
- [ ] Nothing here would embarrass the catalogue in front of a specialist

### 2.8 nuScenes (nuscenes)

`data/benchmarks/vision/nuscenes.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-10-14 · last verified 2026-10-14

*1,000 Boston and Singapore drives with camera, lidar and radar: 3D detection by NDS and more, on hidden test labels.*

A driving dataset from Motional (formerly nuTonomy): 1,000 scenes of 20 seconds, recorded in Boston and Singapore by cars carrying 6 cameras, 5 radars and 1 lidar, annotated at 2 Hz with 3D boxes for 23 classes and their attributes. The headline task is 3D object detection over 10 classes, ranked by the nuScenes Detection Score (NDS), a weighted sum of mean average precision (matched by 2D center distance rather than overlap) and five true-positive error scores for translation, scale, orientation, velocity and attribute. Tracking (AMOTA), trajectory prediction (minADE and minFDE), lidar segmentation (nuScenes-lidarseg, mIoU) and panoptic segmentation and tracking (Panoptic nuScenes, PQ and PAT) were added in dated devkit releases from 2019 to 2021. Train and validation annotations are released and test annotations are not; entrants upload test predictions to an evaluation server, on EvalAI until August 2026 and on Hugging Face since, at most three a year. The maintainers ran challenges at CVPR, ICRA and NeurIPS workshops from 2019 to 2021, and the leaderboards still take entries. The data is free for non-commercial use under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and Motional's terms, after registration.

**Evidence** (57 quoted fields), by checklist area:

#### nuscenes · Identity and id

- `self_description` · [S1][nuscenes-s1]
  > In this work we present nuTonomy scenes (nuScenes), the first dataset to carry the full autonomous vehicle sensor suite: 6 cameras, 5 radars and 1 lidar, all with full 360 degree field of view.
- `released` = 2019-03-26 · [S1][nuscenes-s1]
  > Submitted on 26 Mar 2019
- `release_venue` = CVPR 2020 · [S1][nuscenes-s1]
  > CVPR 2020 camera ready incl. supplementary material

#### nuscenes · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/driving-perception-3d · [S2][nuscenes-s2]
  - why: Every perception task is scored on the road scene around a car, recovered from the car's own cameras, lidar and radar in 3D -- boxes in the global frame, tracks, labels per lidar point. The leaf was created to keep nuScenes' NDS apart from driving scores such as CARLA's.
  > nuScenes is the first large-scale dataset to provide data from the entire sensor suite of an autonomous vehicle (6 cameras, 1 LIDAR, 5 RADAR, GPS, IMU).
- `capability` = perception · [S3][nuscenes-s3]
  - why: Detection, tracking, lidar segmentation and the panoptic tasks score what was recovered from raw camera, lidar and radar data -- 3D boxes with velocities and attributes, tracks, per-point classes -- against held-out labels.
  > The goal of this task is to place a 3D bounding box around 10 different object categories,
- `evaluation_method` = domain-metric, statistical-fit, classification-metric, composite · [S3][nuscenes-s3]
  - why: The detection README defines NDS as a weighted sum of mAP and the five true-positive scores, each computed by its own measure.
  > We then assign a weight of \*5\* to mAP and \*1\* to each of the 5 TP scores and calculate the normalized sum.
- `designed_for_subjects` = task-specific-supervised-model · [S5][nuscenes-s5]
  - why: The entrants are 3D detectors, trackers, segmentation networks and motion forecasters trained on the released train split and scored as trained, from the paper's PointPillars and OFT baselines to today's multi-view camera and lidar-camera fusion detectors.
  > PointPillars, OFT and SSD+3D are baselines provided in this paper, other methods are the top submissions to the nuScenes detection challenge leaderboard.

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `vision/detection` · [S3][nuscenes-s3]
  - why: The detection task localises and labels object instances, but as 3D boxes in the global frame from any of the sensors, while the leaf is defined within an image; driving-perception-3d is the leaf for this case.
  > Here we define the 3D object detection task on nuScenes.
- `domain` not `robotics-embodiment/autonomous-driving-planning` · [S4][nuscenes-s4]
  - why: No task scores a driving outcome. Prediction forecasts other agents' trajectories and scores their displacement from the logged future; nothing drives the car.
  > The goal of the nuScenes prediction task is to predict the future trajectories of objects in the nuScenes dataset.
- `capability` not `probabilistic-forecasting` · [S4][nuscenes-s4]
  - why: Prediction submissions give up to 25 trajectories with probabilities for an agent's next 6 seconds, but the futures are already logged and only withheld, which the term excludes.
  > The user can submit up to 25 proposed future trajectories
- `capability` not `distribution-shift-generalization` · [S5][nuscenes-s5]
  - why: Boston and Singapore, rain and night are in every split in the same proportions; no shifted condition is scored as its own.
  > The dataset splits (train, val, test) follow the same data distribution with respect to these criteria.
- `designed_for_subjects` not `classical-algorithm` · [S6][nuscenes-s6]
  - why: Some tracking entries, such as TrustTrack-UQ, run a deterministic tracker with no learned components, but on top of learned detections, and the benchmark was built for learned perception.
  > The tracker is fully deterministic, with no learned components in the tracking stage.
