**Open review checks** (7):

1. (field `evaluation_method`) evaluation\_method tags NDS's constituents as composite asks. The translation, orientation and velocity errors are read as statistical-fit (mean errors on continuous values) and the attribute error as classification-metric (macro-averaged accuracy). All five TP errors could instead be read as nuScenes-defined detection measures (domain-metric), which would leave composite combining a single method. · [S3][nuscenes-s3]
   > Our final score is a weighted sum of mean Average Precision (mAP) and several True Positive (TP) metrics.
2. (field `subsets`) The prediction subset inherits driving-perception-3d and perception, but it forecasts agents' trajectories from their annotated past and the map, which is not perception. No capability passes. probabilistic-forecasting needs unresolved futures, scientific-prediction is for physical systems, and planning is the ego's own plan. Its challenge also requires a technical report and has the maintainers re-run the top five on the test set. publication-gated and sandboxed-rerun are recorded on the subset only, not tagged on the entry. · [S4][nuscenes-s4]
   > Every submission to the challenge must be accompanied by a brief technical report
3. (field `as_used`) The leaderboard lists PQR3D's camera-only row, which uses future frames, beside entries that keep to the 0.5 s past-data rule. Whether the maintainers enforce the rule or only label such rows decides whether NDS on the board is comparable across rows (as\_used). · [S7][nuscenes-s7]
   > The submitted ViT-L configuration uses future frames and external pretraining.
4. (field `data.data_provenance`) data\_provenance has real-world-instrument only. The labels come from Scale's "expert annotators", but no source describes the annotators' prior skill or training. That would decide between expert-authored and crowd-authored. · [S5][nuscenes-s5]
   > Using expert annotators and multiple validation steps, we achieve highly accurate annotations.
5. (field `activity`) activity leaderboard-live-no-round rests on the 2019-2021 workshop challenges being rounds. If they count as events beside a leaderboard that never ran in rounds, it is accepting-submissions.
6. (field `subsets`) Identity. nuScenes-lidarseg and Panoptic nuScenes are filed as subsets because they share the scenes, splits, devkit and site, though Panoptic nuScenes has its own paper (arXiv 2109.03805, not read). nuImages (2D images, no leaderboard) and nuPlan (planning, its own benchmark) are left out. · [S11][nuscenes-s11]
   > Jul. 29, 2021: Devkit v1.1.6: Panoptic nuScenes v1.0 code, NeurIPS challenge announcement.
7. (field `governance.independence_flags`) maintainer-competes-on-own-benchmark rests on Motional's own rows, one of them marked as a baseline outside the challenge. contamination\_risk medium follows COCO's and ScanNet's reading of released test inputs with withheld labels. · [S7][nuscenes-s7]
   > PointPillars is a baseline that does not participate in the nuScenes detection challenge.

### 2.9 OmniDocBench (omnidocbench)

`data/benchmarks/vision/omnidocbench.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-08 · last verified 2026-11-08

*Full-page PDF parsing scored on recovered text, tables, formulas and reading order against layout-level annotations.*

A benchmark for document parsing: turning a page image into structured, machine-readable content. Each page carries block-level layout boxes (titles, text paragraphs, tables, figures, display formulas, headers and footers, and more), span-level boxes for text lines and inline formulas, reading-order and caption-affiliation annotations, the text of every text region, LaTeX for formulas and both HTML and LaTeX for tables, and page and block attributes (document type, layout, language, watermarks, blurred scans, coloured backgrounds, rotated text, table frames and merged cells). The end-to-end task gives the system the page image and scores the Markdown it returns: text by normalised edit distance, tables by TEDS on HTML, display formulas by CDM, and reading order by edit distance, after an extraction and matching step that pairs the output's elements with the ground truth and ignores headers, footers and captions. Since v1.5 the headline Overall averages the three content scores. The same annotations support single-task evaluations of layout detection, table recognition, formula recognition and detection, and text OCR. v1.0 (CVPR 2025) had 981 pages of nine document types, drawn from over 200,000 web and internal PDFs, pre-annotated by models and corrected by annotators and researchers. v1.5 (September 2025) added 374 pages, and v1.6 (April 2026) a Hard subset of 296 pages and a new matching algorithm, for 1,651 pages in a Base, Hard and Full protocol. The maintainers run the models on the README leaderboard themselves; in November 2026 its top Overall on v1.6 Full is 97.03.

#### omnidocbench · Identity and id

#### omnidocbench · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/document-understanding; secondary vision/ocr-handwriting · [S1][omnidocbench-s1]
  - why: The scored quantity is the structure and content recovered from the page image (its text, tables, formulas and reading order) against annotations of that page, which is document-understanding's own case and vision's inclusion test (what was recovered from an image). No question or description is posed; the only text the system gets is, for a prompted model, an instruction to transcribe. That is where it differs from DocVQA (multimodal/visual-qa), whose items are natural-language questions about a page scored on the answer, so the correspondence between the page and a question is what is measured. Text recognition, including handwritten notes, is scored separately and inside the Overall, so ocr-handwriting is secondary.
  > Document parsing, a core task in computer vision and document intelligence, aims to extract structured, machine-readable content from unstructured documents such as PDFs.
- `capability` = perception · [S1][omnidocbench-s1]
  - why: The input is a rendered page image, and every score measures what was recovered from it, characters, table structure, formula structure and the order of blocks; the paper's analysis is of failures on blurred scans, watermarks, dense newspapers and handwriting.
  > Notably, most VLMs fail to recognize when dealing with the Newspapers
- `evaluation_method` = composite, reference-metric, domain-metric · [S3][omnidocbench-s3]
  - why: Since v1.5 the headline Overall averages three sub-scores produced by different methods. Text is scored by normalised edit distance, a fixed-formula string similarity of the kind reference-metric names. Tables are scored by TEDS, a tree-edit-distance similarity defined for table structure in HTML, and display formulas by CDM, a character-matching metric defined for formula recognition; both are the document-analysis field's own measures with no meaning outside it, so domain-metric. The single-task layout and formula detection subsets use COCO-style mAP, also domain-metric. v1.0's paper reported the sub-scores separately, with no Overall of this form.
  > The \*\*Overall\*\* metric is now calculated as ((1 - text Edit distance) \* 100 + table TEDS + formula CDM) / 3
- `designed_for_subjects` = task-specific-supervised-model, instruction-tuned-model · [S1][omnidocbench-s1]
  - why: The paper's three classes of entrant are pipeline tools built from task-trained layout, OCR, table and formula models, expert vision-language models trained for document parsing (GOT-OCR, Nougat), both scored as trained artefacts on a general perception task, and general vision-language models (GPT-4o, Qwen2-VL-72B, InternVL2-76B) prompted to output the page as Markdown. Document parsing is a general perception task, not a discipline, so domain-specialist-model does not apply.
  > General VLMs: These are general-purpose large multimodal models inherently capable of document parsing.

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `multimodal/visual-qa` · [S3][omnidocbench-s3]
  - why: Rejected under 02 S11 rule 12. document-understanding's not\_to\_be\_confused\_with sends a document-image benchmark posed as questions to visual-qa; OmniDocBench poses none, and its metrics compare the recovered page content with the page's own annotations, not an answer with a question.
  > The evaluation uses the model's Markdown output of the entire PDF page parsing results as the prediction.
- `domain` not `multimodal/chart-diagram-understanding` · [S1][omnidocbench-s1]
  - why: Figures are located by layout boxes but carry no content annotation, so nothing in a chart or diagram is scored.
  > The recognition annotations are also provided for each annotation category except for Figures.
- `capability` not `spatial-reasoning` · [S1][omnidocbench-s1]
  - why: Reading order across columns is scored, but as the edit distance of a recovered sequence against the annotated one, a structure read off the layout; it is not in the Overall, and no item asks for an inference about spatial relations.
  > Reading order is evaluated using the Normalized Edit Distance as metric.
- `evaluation_method` not `model-derived-metric` · [S1][omnidocbench-s1]
  - why: CDM renders the predicted and the reference LaTeX and matches their characters, and no source read says a learned model computes it; TEDS and edit distance are fixed formulas. See the review checks.
  > Formulas are currently evaluated using the Character Detection Matching (CDM) metric \[41\], Normalized Edit Distance, and BLEU \[33\].
- `designed_for_subjects` not `domain-specialist-model` · [S1][omnidocbench-s1]
  - why: The specialised parsers are trained for document parsing, a general perception task with no scientific, clinical or engineering-design discipline, which the term's exclusion test sends to task-specific-supervised-model.
  > Expert VLMs: These are large multimodal models specifically trained for document parsing tasks.

**Open review checks** (10):

1. (field `versions`) v1.0, v1.5 and v1.6 are modelled as editions because each adds pages under the same task, while also correcting earlier annotations and changing the matching. They are supersets, not replacement sets, and v1.6 keeps v1.5 as its Base tier for comparability, so a reviewer could read v1.5 and v1.6 as revisions with additions. Scores across them are not comparable either way. · [S6][omnidocbench-s6]
   > Base (1,355 pages): retains the original v1.5 evaluation set to maintain comparability with historical results.
2. (field `versions`) v1.7 is a version label with no stated change to pages, annotations or scoring, and the leaderboard is still captioned v1.6\_full; the Hugging Face dataset was modified on 2026-06-26, after it. Whether v1.7 changed the data, and whether that later modification is an unannounced change (which would make refresh rolling-live), is not shown by any source read. · [S3][omnidocbench-s3]
   > Updated from \*\*v1.6\*\* to \*\*v1.7\*\*, added the Qianfan-OCR leaderboard, and supported skills-based evaluation.
3. (field `domain`) The domain rests on what is scored. The output is text produced from an image, which a reader could take for multimodal/any-to-any-generation; it is kept in vision because the text is a transcription of the page's own content, as document-understanding and ocr-handwriting define it. DocVQA, by contrast, scores answers to questions and sits in multimodal.
4. (field `activity`) activity no-submission-channel rests on the README, which shows a maintainer-run table and no submission route. The official site on opendatalab.com, which reports cite as the leaderboard, could not be read. If developers can ask to be evaluated or send results, activity is accepting-submissions and submission\_process gains that route.
5. (field `governance.independence_flags`) maintainer-competes-on-own-benchmark rests on the MinerU2.5-Pro report, which both defines v1.6 and ranks the lab's own model first on it, with the Hard pages drawn from that model's data pool. The leaderboard's top is now other models (OXR-1.0 at 97.03), and MinerU2.5-Pro is fifth. · [S3][omnidocbench-s3]
   > OXR-1.0 Specialized VLMs 1.3B 97.03
6. (field `governance.maintainer_type`) maintainer\_type is null. Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory's legal form is not stated in any source read; the field needs a source that states it.
7. (field `evaluation_method`) TEDS and CDM are tagged domain-metric as table- and formula-recognition measures. TEDS is also a similarity against a reference markup, which a reviewer could read as reference-metric; CDM's description was not read beyond the paper's naming of it, so whether any learned model takes part in it (model-derived-metric) is unconfirmed.
8. (field `lineage`) Real5-OmniDocBench is recorded as a fork on the PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 report's description (re-photographed v1.5 pages, the same annotations and protocol). Its own paper (arXiv 2603.04205) was not read, so its maintainer and whether it is a separate benchmark or a test condition of this one are unconfirmed; it has no entry. · [S4][omnidocbench-s4]
   > Each subset maintains a one-to-one correspondence with the original OmniDocBench samples and follows the same ground-truth annotations and evaluation protocols.
9. (field `data.dataset_licence`) dataset\_licence is null. The README limits the dataset to research and non-commercial use without naming a licence, and the Hugging Face record declares none. · [S3][omnidocbench-s3]
   > The dataset is for research purposes only and not for commercial use.
10. (field `data.data_provenance`) data\_provenance crowd-authored rests on the annotators' expertise being undescribed; annotation was supported by 2077AI, and the v1.6 Hard pages by professional teams. The annotations were model pre-annotations corrected by people, which a reviewer may want recorded as model-generated as well. · [S6][omnidocbench-s6]
   > are annotated by professional teams with inter-annotator cross-validation to ensure ground truth quality

- [ ] Identity and id: the name, aliases, id, paper and release date are right, and this is one benchmark, not a family or an edition of another
- [ ] Domain and capabilities: the primary and secondary subdomains, capabilities, evaluation methods and intended subjects fit, and no rejected term should have been kept
- [ ] Task and evaluation: the task, scoring, ground truth, entrants and harness read as the sources describe them
- [ ] Data and licence: access, refresh, provenance, sizes, subsets, contamination and licences match the sources
- [ ] Governance and independence: maintainer type, submission process, funding and independence flags are right
- [ ] Lifecycle and activity: lifecycle, activity, versions, editions and history are current

- [ ] Nothing here would embarrass the catalogue in front of a specialist

### 2.10 MedMNIST (medmnist)

`data/benchmarks/vision/medmnist.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-10 · last verified 2026-11-10

*18 standardised 2D and 3D biomedical image classification datasets at MNIST-like sizes, scored by AUC and accuracy.*

A collection of biomedical image classification datasets from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and collaborators, built so that machine-learning methods can be compared across many small, standardised tasks without medical background knowledge. Version 2 holds 12 2D datasets (MedMNIST2D) and 6 3D datasets (MedMNIST3D), each pre-processed from a published source dataset, or in two cases new data, into 28 x 28 images or 28 x 28 x 28 volumes with a fixed train / validation / test split: pathology patches, chest X-rays, dermatoscopy, retinal OCT and fundus images, breast ultrasound, blood and kidney cell microscopy, abdominal and chest CT, vessel and adrenal shapes and electron microscopy, with binary, multi-class, multi-label and ordinal tasks from 780 to 236,386 samples. A classifier is trained on each dataset's training split and scored on its test split by AUC and accuracy, and methods are compared on those metrics averaged over the 2D and over the 3D datasets. The release baselines are ResNets and three AutoML tools. Version 1 (ISBI 2021) had 10 2D datasets; MedMNIST+ (January 2024) adds 64, 128 and 224 pixel copies of the 2D images and 64-voxel copies of the 3D ones, with the same samples and splits. The data is on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0, except DermaMNIST under CC BY-NC 4.0, and the maintainers say it is not intended for clinical use. There is no leaderboard; results appear in their authors' papers.

#### medmnist · Identity and id

#### medmnist · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary vision/medical-imaging-cv; secondary vision/classification, medicine-health/medical-imaging-diagnostic · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: The benchmark's own claim is a machine-learning one. Its authors built it as a VDD-like decathlon that isolates the learning algorithm from the end-to-end pipeline, standardised so that no background knowledge is needed, and they disclaim clinical use. That is medical-imaging-cv's inclusion test (a vision method, medical images as the test domain, no clinical task claimed). Both leaves say the claim decides and the metric does not. The exclusion test (clinically defined targets against a clinician reference standard) is met by some datasets' labels taken over from their sources, such as DermaMNIST's diagnoses, RetinaMNIST's retinopathy grades and NoduleMNIST3D's malignancy levels. It is not met by others. TissueMNIST and BloodMNIST are bioimage cell types, SynapseMNIST3D is rat neurons, OrganMNIST's labels are organs, and ChestMNIST's disease labels were text-mined from reports. MedMNIST also downsamples to 28 pixels, merges classes and scores no result against a clinical reference of its own, so medical-imaging-diagnostic is secondary, for the datasets whose labels are diagnoses or findings (review\_checks). vision/classification names the operation, every task assigning a whole image or volume to classes, and is secondary to the more specific medical-imaging-cv.
  > Therefore, a large but simple dataset focusing on the machine learning part like VDD, rather than the end-to-end system like MSD, will serve as a better benchmark to evaluate the generalization performance of the machine learning algorithms on the medical image analysis tasks.
- `capability` = perception · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: The input is a small medical or biological image or volume and the score measures whether the class recovered from it matches the label.
  > so that no background knowledge is required for users
- `evaluation_method` = classification-metric, exact-match · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: Both metrics are reported for every dataset and averaged. AUC is a statistic of the score ranking against the labels, which is classification-metric. ACC is the share of test images whose predicted label equals the ground truth, a mean of per-item verdicts, which the exact-match test keeps for accuracy against a fixed label set. Neither is named the headline.
  > Area under ROC curve (AUC)44 and Accuracy (ACC) are used as the evaluation metrics.
- `designed_for_subjects` = task-specific-supervised-model · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: Entrants are classifiers trained on each dataset's training split and scored as trained, and AutoML tools refitted on each dataset, which the term's inclusion test places here. The release baselines are ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 (2D, and 2.5D, 3D and ACS convolutions in 3D), auto-sklearn, AutoKeras and Google AutoML Vision.
  > We benchmark several standard deep learning methods and AutoML tools with MedMNIST v2 on both 2D and 3D datasets

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `medicine-health/medical-imaging-segmentation` · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: NoduleMNIST3D's source supports segmentation, and AdrenalMNIST3D and VesselMNIST3D are built from shape masks, but every MedMNIST task is a classification of the whole image or volume; nothing is scored as a mask.
  > The AdrenalMNIST3D is a new 3D shape classification dataset
- `capability` not `distribution-shift-generalization` · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: PathMNIST's test patches come from a different clinical centre than its training patches, but that is one dataset's split, not a shifted condition scored apart from an in-distribution one; every other dataset uses its source's split or a random 7:1:2 split. MedMNIST-C, the corrupted derivative by other authors, scores that shift (lineage).
  > and a test dataset (CRC-VAL-HE-7K) of 7,180 image patches from a different clinical center
- `capability` not `sample-efficiency` · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: Dataset sizes range from hundreds to hundreds of thousands of samples, and small datasets are part of the design, but no fixed sample budget is set and scored.
  > Data users are also encouraged to analyze the average performance over the 12 2D datasets and 6 3D datasets to benchmark their methods.
- `evaluation_method` not `ordinal-grading` · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: RetinaMNIST is an ordinal-regression task (five retinopathy grades), but the result is still a number, AUC or ACC, not a band.
  > The task is ordinal regression for 5-level grading of diabetic retinopathy severity.
- `designed_for_subjects` not `domain-specialist-model` · [S3][medmnist-s3]
  - why: The tasks come from medicine and biology, but the benchmark is built so that general methods can be compared without domain knowledge, and its baselines are general architectures and AutoML tools. The README suggests MedMNIST+ as a resource for medical foundation models, which no source read scores.
  > As a complement to the previous 28-size MedMNIST, the large-size version could serve as a standardized benchmark for medical foundation models.

#### medmnist · Task and evaluation

- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system Google AutoML Vision (Edge models) · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  > For MedMNIST2D, Google AutoML Vision outperforms all the other methods in average AUC, however, it is very close to the performance of baseline ResNets.
- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system ResNet-50 with 3D convolutions · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  > Surprisingly, the ResNet-50 with standard 3D convolution outperforms all the other methods on average.
- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system LiteMed-ViT · [S5][medmnist-s5]
  > Evaluated against three compact CNN baselines on three MedMNIST subsets of varying modality and class balance, LiteMed-ViT attains higher accuracy than all three baselines on BloodMNIST (95.05%) and two on PathMNIST (89.15%).
- `learned_entrant_evidence` = system ConvNeXt-Tiny shared backbone with label smoothing · [S4][medmnist-s4]
  > Our best configuration, a ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone with label smoothing
- `ground_truth_source` = held-out-labels · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: The labels are taken from the sources except where a task was simplified for the small images.
  > The MedMNIST uses the classification labels from the source datasets directly in most cases, but the labels could be simplified (merged or deleted classes) if the classification tasks on the small images are too difficult.
- `reproducible_by_third_party` = true · [S3][medmnist-s3]
  - why: Anyone can download every dataset with its test labels from Zenodo, train on the official split and score with the maintainers' evaluator; no step needs the maintainers.
  > Each subset (e.g., \`pathmnist.npz\`) is comprised of 6 keys: \`train\_images\`, \`train\_labels\`, \`val\_images\`, \`val\_labels\`, \`test\_images\` and \`test\_labels\`.
- `task` = exists true; input a 28 x 28 grey or RGB image (MedMNIST2D) or a 28 x 28 x 28 volume (MedMNIST3D); in MedMNIST+ also 64, 128 or 224 pixels (2D) or 64 voxels (3D); output Class scores and a predicted label for the dataset's task (binary, multi-class, ordinal, or 14 binary labels for ChestMNIST).; scoring AUC and accuracy on each dataset's official test split, and their means over the 12 2D datasets and over the 6 3D datasets. The paper reports the mean of at least three runs per method.; metric_range 0, 1 · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  > Thereby, we report average AUC and ACC score over MedMNIST2D and MedMNIST3D respectively to easily compare the performance of different methods.
- `execution.reproducibility_tier` = fully-automatable · [S3][medmnist-s3]
  - why: The data with test labels is public, the splits are fixed, and the maintainers' evaluator computes AUC and ACC from a result file, so anyone can produce the scores with no human or maintainer step.
  > Parse and evaluate a standard result file
- `execution.harness` = The medmnist Python package's Evaluator (medmnist/evaluator.py; python -m medmnist evaluate) · [S3][medmnist-s3]
  > \[\`evaluator.py\`\](medmnist/evaluator.py): Standardized evaluation functions.
- `aggregation_policy` = official-aggregate · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: The averages are the maintainers' own comparison of methods.
  > Thereby, we report average AUC and ACC score over MedMNIST2D and MedMNIST3D respectively to easily compare the performance of different methods.

#### medmnist · Data and licence

- `as_used` = protocol One shared backbone with a linear head per dataset, trained on 11 MedMNIST datasets together and scored by the harmonic mean of per-task macro-F1 on a competition leaderboard, not the paper's per-dataset AUC and ACC or their averages. · [S4][medmnist-s4]
  > We study 11 heterogeneous MedMNIST datasets using the harmonic mean of per-task macro-F1.
- `as_used` = protocol Accuracy and balanced accuracy on three of the 2D datasets (BloodMNIST, PathMNIST, DermaMNIST), at several input resolutions up to 224 pixels, the MedMNIST+ sizes, and again under MedMNIST-C corruptions. · [S5][medmnist-s5]

#### medmnist · Governance and independence

- `governance.maintainer` = The MedMNIST team (Shanghai Jiao Tong University and collaborators) · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: The data, the repository (the MedMNIST GitHub organisation) and the site are the paper authors'. The corresponding author and the funding are Shanghai Jiao Tong University's, and the paper's authors come from six institutions. No source read names one institution as the holder.
  > This work was also supported by Grant YG2021ZD18 from Shanghai Jiao Tong University Medical Engineering Cross Research.
- `governance.submission_process` = literature-only · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  > Data users are also encouraged to analyze the average performance over the 12 2D datasets and 6 3D datasets to benchmark their methods.
- `governance.independence_flags` = flag no-known-conflict · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  > The authors declare no competing interests.
- `governance.funding` · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  > This work was supported by National Science Foundation of China (U20B200011, 61976137).
- `governance.known_limitation` · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  > Please note that this dataset is NOT intended for clinical use, as substantially reducing the resolution of medical images might result in images that are insufficient to represent and capture different disease pathologies.

#### medmnist · Lifecycle and activity

- `lifecycle` = active · [S5][medmnist-s5]
  - why: Results are still produced against the datasets; a paper submitted on 2026-10-24 reports accuracy on BloodMNIST and PathMNIST, and one from September 2026 on 11 datasets in a competition.
  > Evaluated against three compact CNN baselines on three MedMNIST subsets of varying modality and class balance, LiteMed-ViT attains higher accuracy than all three baselines on BloodMNIST (95.05%) and two on PathMNIST (89.15%).
- `activity` = no-submission-channel · [S1][medmnist-s1]
  - why: The maintainers publish the data, an evaluation script and their own baseline tables, and no leaderboard, server or submission route; users score their own runs and report them in their papers. The multi-task competition in as\_used is a third party's.
  > The data API and evaluation script in Python is available at https://github.com/MedMNIST/MedMNIST.

**Open review checks** (10):

1. (field `domain`) Primary domain. The claim test gives vision/medical-imaging-cv (a machine-learning decathlon needing no background knowledge, disclaimed for clinical use). But most 2D datasets and NoduleMNIST3D, FractureMNIST3D and AdrenalMNIST3D carry clinically defined targets (diagnoses, retinopathy grades, malignancy, fracture types, adrenal masses), which the vision exclusion test sends to medicine-health "whatever the metric". Confirm that the claim outranks the targets here, or move the primary to medicine-health/medical-imaging-diagnostic. Per-subset domain\_overrides for the clinical datasets are a middle course that was not taken. · [S1][medmnist-s1]
   > Please note that this dataset is NOT intended for clinical use, as substantially reducing the resolution of medical images might result in images that are insufficient to represent and capture different disease pathologies.
2. (field `ground_truth_source`) The reference standard is not uniform. ChestMNIST's labels were text-mined from reports, AdrenalMNIST3D was labelled by one endocrinologist for this release, and SynapseMNIST3D by three neuroscience experts. The other sources' annotation protocols were not read, so which datasets meet "clinicians set the reference standard" is not established. · [S1][medmnist-s1]
   > with the text-mined 14 disease labels, which could be formulized as a multi-label binary-class classification task
3. (field `data.size`) The 3D total differs between sources. The paper and the v2 PDF give 9,998 volumes, the arXiv abstract field 10,214, and the site's data file sums to 9,996 after v2.2. The 10,214 is not explained in any source read. · [S7][medmnist-s7]
   > The resulting dataset, consisting of 708,069 2D images and 10,214 3D images in total
4. (field `versions`) Versions. v1 and v2.0 are editions (new datasets), and v2.1, v2.2 and v3.0 revisions. v2.2 is marked breaking because the OrganCMNIST and OrganSMNIST test splits lost samples. v3.0 (MedMNIST+) adds larger copies of the same samples and splits and is non-breaking for the 28-size files. The README presents it as a benchmark for medical foundation models, which could argue for a variant; the 04 S4 test (same items, same maintainer) points to a revision. v1's Zenodo repository, its date and its 10 datasets' splits were not read. · [S11][medmnist-s11]
   > The data in MedMNIST+ directly corresponds to that of MedMNIST, maintaining the same dataset splits (i.e., train, val, and test) and sample indices.
5. (field `subsets`) Subsets. The 18 datasets are subsets under the two averaged groups, with each dataset's current test count (after v2.2) as items. Whether 20 subset records are the wanted granularity, or the two groups alone, is a judgement.
6. (field `governance.maintainer_type`) maintainer\_type academic-lab or community-collective. The GitHub organisation and Zenodo record span six institutions with no stated holder; the corresponding author, the funding and the first affiliation are Shanghai Jiao Tong University's. · [S1][medmnist-s1]
   > This work was also supported by Grant YG2021ZD18 from Shanghai Jiao Tong University Medical Engineering Cross Research.
7. (field `governance.independence_flags`) no-known-conflict rests on the paper's competing-interests statement, its funding lines and the absence of any stated support from Google, whose commercial AutoML service is a baseline. The release papers' baselines are the maintainers' own, without a ranking. · [S1][medmnist-s1]
   > The authors declare no competing interests.
8. (field `data.upstream_licences`) Upstream licences. The paper says some sources are CC BY-NC and were redistributed with permission, but not which; only DermaMNIST is listed as CC BY-NC. No source dataset's own terms (NIH-ChestXray14, HAM10000, LIDC-IDRI, LiTS, RibFrac, IntrA and the rest) were read. · [S1][medmnist-s1]
   > All source datasets are either associated with the Creative Commons (CC) Licenses or developed by us, which allows us to develop derivative datasets based on them.
9. (field `execution.harness_availability`) official-harness rests on the README's description of the package's evaluator and its evaluate command. The code was not read, and the paper's own baselines ran from the separate experiments repository. If the evaluator is a convenience rather than the scoring path, reference-implementation-only fits. · [S3][medmnist-s3]
   > \[\`evaluator.py\`\](medmnist/evaluator.py): Standardized evaluation functions.
10. (field `as_used`) Current papers rarely use the paper's protocol (per-dataset AUC and ACC, 2D and 3D averages, 28 pixels).
